changes: p1 Dharmasena: roles reduced to owner (the copy was written and given to him: 'cosyaṃ biyā'; nothing beyond receipt marks him as beneficiary); confidence lowered to medium, since the colophon reads 'dharmasyaṇa' and 'Dharmasena' is the cataloguer's normalization
residence 'madhyapurī' stated more cautiously: in the text it stands before both names, so it may be the place of copying rather than Dharmasena's residence
date month/weekday normalized (phālguna, budha); ce_approx 1587 confirmed (NS 707+880; Phālguna falls in Feb/Mar 1587)
purpose rephrased; notes extended about the second-hand addition

relations.evidence: dharmasyaṇajuyātaṃ cosyaṃ biyā, likhita vajracārya udayacandrajusyaṃ biyā

purpose: written by Udayacandra and given to Dharmasena (parārtha)
notes: The catalogue names Dharmasena Vajrācārya as the scribe, but the Newari text says the copy was written and given to Vajrācārya Dharmasyaṇa/Dharmasena ('cosyaṃ biyā') and that the writing was done and handed over by Vajrācārya Udayacandra ('likhita ... udayacandrajusyaṃ biyā juro'). So Udayacandra is the scribe. 'Dharmasyaṇa' is a Newari spelling of Dharmasena; this reading is probable but not certain. 'Madhyapurī' stands before both names: it could be the place of copying or where the two men lived. The verses added later in a second hand (Vārāhī stotra/mantras) name no persons.
